title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: Advanced review set explorer for KQL analysis (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, preview behaviour, access controls and premium licensing statements are supported. Minor corrections should include the omitted heading in the permissions path and remove the checklist instruction to review case membership, which has no corresponding control row.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Older review sets can produce column not found errors for properties unavailable when their data was generated.
claims.quote: Some older review sets might not support certain KQL properties if those properties weren't available when the review set was created and data was generated. Querying an unsupported property in an older review set results in a column not found error.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn's remedy for unsupported properties in older review sets is a new review set with Add to review set to regenerate data.
claims.quote: To resolve this error, create a new review set and use the Add to review set process to regenerate the data with the latest supported properties.

claims.claim: The explorer's Learn page does not state cloud availability or rollout dates for GCC, GCC High and DoD.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record does not state a default, rollout mechanics or licensing.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: What the government-cloud change does on arrival without administrator action is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" enable default disable; read roadmap, edisc-review-set-explorer and edisc-settings-review-sets. Preview navigation is documented, but no arrival default for the planned government-cloud release.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no explorer-only administrator switch in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" enable default disable; "Advanced review set explorer" PowerShell configuration setting disable. Read explorer, permissions and review-set settings pages; results identify access roles and grouping, not an explorer-only switch.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Explorer queries run against the current review set's indexed items, rather than adding another data source.
claims.quote: All queries in the Advanced review set explorer (preview) run against the current review set's indexed items. You don't need to specify a table name. The review set acts as the default data source.

claims.claim: The condition builder and explorer query the same review set content.
claims.quote: Search and filter content using the query condition builder to focus on specific subsets of documents. Use the Advanced review set explorer (preview) to run Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries directly against review set data

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: KQL can group and count items per participant.
claims.quote: The following example expands the Participants field so each participant appears on its own row, then counts the number of items associated with each participant.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn's explorer examples extract and list external recipient addresses for each item.
claims.quote: Find all review set items that include at least one external recipient (outside your organization contoso.com), and list those external email addresses for each item.

claims.claim: Learn's explorer examples expose participant information per item.
claims.quote: Find items exchanged exclusively between two specific users - John and David - with no other participants. This query isolates their direct one-to-one communications and shows only three properties: subject title, sender, and recipients.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Opening the explorer requires an account assigned eDiscovery permissions and access to the case's review set.
claims.quote: sign in with the credentials for a user account assigned eDiscovery permissions. Select the eDiscovery solution card, and then select Cases in the left navigation. Select a case, and then select the Review sets tab.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Review role lets users access review sets in cases they are members of.
claims.quote: This role lets users access review sets in eDiscovery. Users who are assigned this role can see and open the list of cases that they're members of.

claims.claim: General eDiscovery review set access governs access to the explorer rather than acting as an explorer-only switch.
claims.quote: sign in with the credentials for a user account assigned eDiscovery permissions. Select a review set, and then select the Advanced review set explorer (preview) tab.

claims.claim: Learn describes no autonomous action taken by the explorer.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" enable disable default admin setting license meter audit; read entire edisc-review-set-explorer. Documented actions are user-run, read-only queries and visualisations; no autonomous action described.

claims.claim: Adding data to a review set can change query results because results reflect its current indexed state.
claims.quote: Results reflect the current indexed state of the review set. If you add more data to the review set, the query might return different results.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The included licensing model reflects the product's E5 subscription or related add-on entitlement for premium eDiscovery capabilities.
claims.quote: If your organization has an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 subscription (or related E5 add-on subscriptions), you can further manage cases and analyze content by using premium eDiscovery features.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A user whose data is analysed with premium features needs Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5, or eligible E1/E3 with Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license. Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite

claims.claim: Case-member administrators, compliance officers and legal personnel using premium features to collect, view and analyse data do not need an E5 licence.
claims.quote: Administrators, compliance officers, or legal personnel who are assigned to cases as members and use premium eDiscovery features to collect, view, and analyze data don't need an E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The explorer page states no licence or meter, and no explorer-specific price, licence or meter is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" license billing; read edisc-review-set-explorer, edisc, edisc-permissions, edisc-features-components and edisc-billing. Premium entitlement is documented; no separate explorer licence, query meter or price.

claims.claim: Reviewer is a role group that can assign eDiscovery-related permissions.
claims.quote: On the Role groups page in the Microsoft Purview portal, you can also assign users eDiscovery-related permissions by adding them to the Compliance Administrator, Organization Management, and Reviewer role groups.

claims.claim: Review access can be assigned in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. On the eDiscovery Manager pane ... Select Edit. On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Use 'Settings > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups' in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table; the omitted text is a heading, not a missing selectable navigation step.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> in Security & Compliance PowerShell adds a mail-enabled security group to the eDiscovery Manager subgroup.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup ... by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell. Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, case membership
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to check case membership, but the controls table covers role-group membership only.
claims.quote: Confirm which cases your reviewers work in and who is a member ... Controls: Who can access review sets, and so the explorer, through eDiscovery roles.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Confirm which cases your reviewers work in and who is a member, because the explorer opens from a case's review sets.' It asks readers to check a control absent from the table; do not add a new row in this correction.

claims.claim: Learn says eDiscovery Managers can access and manage only the cases they create.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.

claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions in the portal requires Organization Management role-group membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The explorer has a Getting started tab with KQL reference material.
claims.quote: The Getting started tab below the query results area provides a quick reference for building queries. It includes selectable examples organized into two categories.

claims.claim: The explorer provides Sample queries.
